title: Finding Skilled Tradesmen: How to Hire the Best
meta_description: How to find skilled tradesmen: write a brief that says what you need, use your network properly, judge the soft skills, and screen before anyone starts.
h1: Finding Skilled Tradesmen: How to Hire the Best
hero_subtitle: A practical guide to hiring trades who are reliable as well as capable.

intro.answer: Finding skilled tradesmen starts with being clear about what you are actually looking for. A brief that specifies the work, the qualifications and the standard is what makes it possible to judge anyone against it.

image.alt: Skilled tradesmen working together on a construction project

intro.roadmap: This guide covers four things: defining your requirements properly, using your network rather than starting cold, evaluating the soft skills that decide whether someone fits, and screening effectively before anyone sets foot on site.

briefing.title: Write the Brief Before You Ask Around
briefing.intro: Most hiring in construction starts with a phone call to someone who might know someone. That works when you already know exactly what you need. When you do not, it delivers whoever was available, and you find out the difference on site.

panels.heading: What should the brief actually contain?
paragraphs: The project specifics: what the work is, the standard expected, and the timescale. Then the qualifications the job genuinely requires.

Be precise about that last one. Some trades have no formal entry requirements, while others need specific certifications, and assuming either way is how you end up with a problem on a job that gets inspected.

panels.heading: Then judge more than the trade skill
paragraphs: Technical ability gets someone through the gate. Everything else decides whether you would put them in front of a client.
steps: Write the brief, including qualifications and the standard of finish.
Use your network first, because a recommendation carries information a CV does not.
Evaluate the soft skills: reliability, communication, and how they handle being told something is wrong.
Screen properly before anyone starts, not after the first week.

review.label: Worth remembering
review.text: Reliability is worth more than raw skill on most jobs. A very good tradesman who turns up when he feels like it will cost you more than a solid one who always does.
